title: Linux Package Management: apt, dnf and Beyond
summary: Quick revision notes on Linux package managers: apt vs dnf, update vs upgrade, everyday install/remove/search commands, repositories and keys, dpkg and rpm queries, snaps and flatpaks, and building from source.

chapters.title: Package Managers: The Mental Model
points: A package manager resolves dependencies, downloads signed packages from repositories and records installed files in a local database
Debian family (Ubuntu, Mint): apt on top of dpkg, .deb packages; RHEL family (Fedora, Rocky, Alma): dnf on top of rpm, .rpm packages
Two layers: low-level dpkg/rpm install one local file with no dependency resolution; high-level apt/dnf fetch from repos and resolve dependencies
Repo metadata is a cached index of available packages and versions; installs use this cache, not the live server
Interview Point: Why does installing a .deb with dpkg -i fail on missing dependencies while apt install succeeds? What is the difference between apt and apt-get? What does dnf use under the hood?

chapters.title: Core Workflow: Update, Upgrade and Install
points: apt update only refreshes the package index; it installs nothing. apt upgrade installs newer versions of installed packages
apt upgrade never removes packages; apt full-upgrade (dist-upgrade) may remove or add packages to resolve changed dependencies
dnf has no separate refresh step: dnf upgrade (alias update) refreshes metadata and upgrades; dnf check-update lists pending updates
Safe order on Debian: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade, then sudo apt install pkg; installing from a stale index gives 404 or old versions
Both need root: sudo apt install -y nginx / sudo dnf install -y nginx; -y auto-confirms prompts
Interview Point: What is the difference between apt update and apt upgrade? When would you use full-upgrade? Does dnf need a separate update-index command?

chapters.title: Everyday Commands: Install, Remove, Search
points: Search: apt search kw / dnf search kw; details: apt show pkg / dnf info pkg; list installed: apt list --installed / dnf list installed
Remove: apt remove keeps config files, apt purge deletes them too; dnf remove has no purge distinction
apt autoremove / dnf autoremove delete dependencies no longer needed by any installed package
Pin a version: apt install pkg=1.2.3-1; dnf install pkg-1.2.3; hold with apt-mark hold pkg or dnf versionlock
Find which package owns a command or file: apt-file search path or dnf provides */bin/tool; clean cache with apt clean / dnf clean all
Interview Point: What is the difference between remove and purge? What does autoremove delete? How do you find which package provides a missing file?

chapters.title: Repositories, Keys, dpkg and rpm Queries
points: Debian repos: /etc/apt/sources.list and /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.list or .sources; RHEL repos: /etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo with baseurl and gpgcheck=1
Repo signing keys verify package authenticity: store per-repo key in /etc/apt/keyrings/ and reference with signed-by=; apt-key is deprecated; dnf imports the gpgkey URL or rpm --import
Adding a third-party repo: add key, add source file, then apt update / dnf makecache; disable temporarily with dnf --disablerepo=name or by removing the source file
dpkg queries: dpkg -l (list), dpkg -L pkg (files in package), dpkg -S /path (which package owns file), dpkg -i file.deb (install local file)
rpm queries: rpm -qa (list all), rpm -ql pkg (files), rpm -qf /path (owner of file), rpm -qi pkg (info), rpm -ivh file.rpm (install local file)
Interview Point: Where are apt and dnf repositories configured? Why was apt-key deprecated? How do you find which package installed a given file on Ubuntu vs Rocky?

chapters.title: Snaps, Flatpaks and Building from Source
points: Snap (Canonical, snapd) and Flatpak (Flathub) bundle an app with its dependencies in a sandbox, so it runs on any distro; cost is larger size and slower first start
Snap: snap install pkg, snap list, snap refresh (auto-updates in background), snap remove pkg; Flatpak: flatpak install flathub org.app.Name, flatpak run, flatpak update
Source build flow: install build tools (build-essential or Development Tools group), then ./configure, make, sudo make install
Prefer ./configure --prefix=/usr/local or checkinstall so files stay out of package-managed paths; make install tracks nothing, so uninstall needs make uninstall or the original source tree
Prefer order: distro repo package, then snap/flatpak, then source build; source builds get no automatic security updates
Interview Point: Why might a snap start slower than a deb? What does make install not do that apt install does? When is building from source justified?

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: apt vs dnf
points: Refresh and upgrade: apt update / apt upgrade vs dnf upgrade (dnf check-update to preview)
Install, remove, purge: apt install|remove|purge pkg vs dnf install|remove pkg; cleanup with autoremove
Search and inspect: apt search|show vs dnf search|info; file owner: dpkg -S vs rpm -qf, dnf provides
Local file and list: dpkg -i / dpkg -l vs rpm -ivh / rpm -qa; files in package: dpkg -L vs rpm -ql
Config locations: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ vs /etc/yum.repos.d/; snap install, flatpak install; source: ./configure && make && sudo make install
Interview Point: Translate apt install, apt search and dpkg -S to the dnf/rpm equivalents. Which commands change the system vs only read it?
